heard: Half of your body's atoms came from distant galaxies. Up to 50% of the Milky Way originated outside our galaxy. Edwin Hubble proved other galaxies existed back in the 1920s. Our solar system takes over 200 million years to orbit the galaxy. At the center sits Sagittarius A star, a supermassive black hole. NASA's Chandra Observatory caught it unleashing a flare 400 times brighter than normal. Powerful intergalactic winds blew massive amounts of matter between galaxies. That dust built our planet, our sun, and us. That is why half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies.
